equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-01.target: I can use fraction bars and number lines to show that two fractions are equivalent because they are the same size or the same point.
equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-01.ifCorrect: You can do this: can use fraction bars and number lines to show that two fractions are equivalent because they are the same size or the same point.
equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-01.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Comparing pictures of different-size wholes, or thinking fractions with different numbers can never be equal. Try this: Line up fraction strips of the same whole; equivalent fractions end at the same place.

equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-02.target: I can write a simple equivalent fraction (halves, thirds, fourths, sixths, eighths) and explain why it is equivalent with a model.
equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-02.ifCorrect: You can do this: can write a simple equivalent fraction (halves, thirds, fourths, sixths, eighths) and explain why it is equivalent with a model.
equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-02.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Adding the same number to the numerator and denominator (1/2 = 2/3). Try this: Split each part of a model into the same number of smaller parts and recount the parts.

equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-03.target: I can write a whole number as a fraction and recognize fractions such as 6/3 or 4/4 that equal whole numbers.
equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-03.ifCorrect: You can do this: can write a whole number as a fraction and recognize fractions such as 6/3 or 4/4 that equal whole numbers.
equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-03.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Thinking 1 = 1/1 only, or that 3/1 means one‑third. Try this: Show 3 wholes each cut into 1 part (3/1) and 1 whole cut into 4 parts with all shaded (4/4).

equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-04.skill: Comparing Fractions with the Same Denominator
equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-04.target: I can compare two fractions with the same denominator by comparing numerators, record with >, =, <, and justify with a model.
equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-04.ifCorrect: You can do this: can compare two fractions with the same denominator by comparing numerators, record with >, =, <, and justify with a model.
equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-04.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Forgetting that the comparison only works when both fractions refer to the same whole. Try this: Use same-size fraction bars; same-size pieces means more pieces is more.

equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-05.skill: Comparing Fractions with the Same Numerator
equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-05.target: I can compare two fractions with the same numerator by reasoning about the size of the pieces and justify with a model.
equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-05.ifCorrect: You can do this: can compare two fractions with the same numerator by reasoning about the size of the pieces and justify with a model.
equivalent-comparing-fractions-skill-05.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Thinking the fraction with the larger denominator is larger (1/8 > 1/4 because 8 > 4). Try this: Share one sandwich among 4 people and among 8 people: who gets the bigger piece?
